newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan oil workers mulling strike - union.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan oil workers mulling strike - union.

text.p: Venezuela's oil worker unions have not ruled out calling a strike over a planned restructuring of state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA), a top union official said Tuesday.
"Right now that possibility (a strike) is not ruled out," Fedepetrol President Carlos Ortega told Reuters.
The reorganization of PDVSA -- under which the holding company's three main subsidiaries are to be dissolved and three function-specific units created -- will cost 12,000 jobs, Ortega said.
"This process of restructuring...will lead to the firing of workers and early retirements," he said.
PDVSA officials, who announced the restructuring plan earlier this month, have said it will save the company $12 billion over 10 years but deny that it will cost jobs.
Ortega was speaking before a meeting with PDVSA President Luis Giusti and Federico Ramirez Leon, head of CTV, Venezuela's largest labor union.
After the meeting to discuss the job implications of the PDVSA re-organization, Fedepetrol officials would meet to decide whether to call a strike, he said.
Fedepetrol represents the majority of Venezuela's roughly 40,000 unionized oil workers. Another roughly 60,000 contract workers work in the industry.
